clue.text: Attention in class! Get prepared for action!

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside another, here the attention placed within the class

parts.note: a class at school is a form
to lend an ear is to pay attention, so ear stands for attention

explanation.surface: A teacher barks at a class to pay attention and get ready for some activity.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation marks make it read like a teacher shouting orders at a class, but 'class' is a school form and 'Attention' is an ear lent to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To arm yourself in advance is to make ready beforehand for a coming fight or challenge.

clue.text: Inside revolutionary joint there's a scuffle

indicators.note: inside means the article goes within the turned joint
revolutionary means turned round, so the joint is read backwards

parts.note: a scarf is a carpentry joint where two timbers are bevelled and overlapped

explanation.surface: A brawl breaks out in a joint full of revolutionaries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns SCARF to FRACS, and A goes inside before the S. 'joint' suggests a dive, but it is the woodworking joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy brawl or quarrel is a scuffle.

clue.text: He's more ashen but Henry's denied upsetting medical problem

indicators.note: upsetting in a down clue turns the letters upside down, reading from bottom to top
denied means a piece is refused, so it is taken out

parts.note: taken as he and s
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
paler means more ashen

explanation.surface: A man looks paler still, though Henry won't admit his worrying illness.
explanation.walkthrough: HES PALER loses its H ('denied') to give ESPALER, which 'upsetting' turns over.
explanation.definitionFit: A relapse is a return of illness after apparent recovery, a medical setback.

clue.text: Sat awkwardly on rickety ladder with legs wide apart

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the first piece sits above the second
awkwardly suggests the letters of the first word sit in a clumsy new order
rickety means unsteady, so the letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: Someone perched clumsily on a wobbly ladder with legs splayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkwardly' makes AST from SAT; 'rickety' makes RADDLE from LADDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting astride something with one leg either side means having the legs spread apart.

clue.text: Ship that stops some undesirable types going off

definitions.text: Ship that stops some undesirable types going off

parts.words: Ship that stops some undesirable types going off
parts.note: the undesirable types are explosive devices at sea, and going off means exploding, not leaving

explanation.surface: A vessel prevents unwelcome people from leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undesirable types going off' sounds like people departing; it means explosives detonating.
explanation.definitionFit: A naval vessel that clears explosive devices from the sea stops them blowing up ships.

clue.text: Rob, little chap quietly painting

parts.note: Des is a short form of the man's name Desmond
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
an oil is an oil painting

explanation.surface: A small man is robbed while he quietly works on a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To plunder or strip a place of its valuables is to rob it.

clue.text: River not shallow but bottomless

indicators.note: bottomless in a down clue means the last letter is removed

parts.note: deep is the opposite of shallow

explanation.surface: A river that is not shallow but has no bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dee is a river in Scotland, and another flows through Wales and Chester.

clue.text: Hack's salary

definitions.meaning: an old worn-out horse, a nag, is called a hack

explanation.definitionFit: This word is old slang both for a broken-down horse and for wages or pay.

clue.text: Being tested, gets nothing right in Latin sadly

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A pupil gets nothing right in a Latin exam, alas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' mixes O, R and LATIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Undergoing a trial or test, like a product on approval, means being tested.

clue.text: Desperate action of smokers facing imminent ban?

definitions.text: Desperate action of smokers facing imminent ban?

parts.words: Desperate action of smokers facing imminent ban?
parts.note: a final desperate effort, read playfully as smokers' final drag before smoking is outlawed

explanation.surface: Smokers grab one more puff before a coming prohibition.
explanation.definitionFit: A final desperate effort made at the point of collapse is an idiom for a desperate action.

clue.text: A local with ten getting drunk suddenly

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so the letters reel into a new order

explanation.surface: A pub regular downs ten drinks and is abruptly intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal 'getting drunk' mixes the letters of A LOCAL plus TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening all in one moment, without warning, happens abruptly.

clue.text: Report of privileges in these offices

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so we want a word that sounds like the next word

parts.note: rights are entitlements or privileges

explanation.surface: An account of the perks enjoyed by staff in a particular set of offices.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text has a stray 'a' that the page does not print. 'Offices' here are church services, not workplaces.
explanation.definitionFit: Religious ceremonies such as the daily services of the church are called offices.

clue.text: Top star makes a record that's funny!

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record
ha is the laugh at something funny

explanation.surface: A leading celebrity releases an album that turns out to be amusing.
explanation.walkthrough: In astronomy the brightest star of a constellation is labelled with the first Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief or brightest star in a constellation carries this Greek-letter label.

clue.text: Slow progress admitted by Carol, not writing properly

indicators.note: something admitted is let inside, so the slow movement goes into the carol word

parts.note: to carol is to sing
a crawl is very slow progress

explanation.surface: Carol is slow to get on with things and her handwriting is untidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a woman's name but is the verb to sing.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing in a hurried, untidy, barely legible hand is exactly a failure to write neatly.

clue.text: Tenet master put out in a fresh formulation?

indicators.note: put out means disturbed, so the letters are put into disorder

explanation.surface: A doctrine is upset by a schoolmaster in a new phrasing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' mixes the letters of TENET MASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something again in new words is a fresh formulation of it.

clue.text: Old documents providing various local addresses

indicators.note: various suggests different arrangements, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A set of ancient papers supplies a range of neighbourhood addresses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' mixes the letters of LOCAL ADDRESSES.
explanation.definitionFit: These ancient Hebrew manuscripts found near Qumran are among the most famous old documents.

clue.text: Yielding with little resistance, say, when about to retire

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for resistance in physics

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round another, here the example abbreviation round the bedtime phrase

parts.note: eg (for example) is what say means
to turn in is to retire to bed

explanation.surface: Someone gives way without much fuss when it is time to go to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link; 'about' puts EG around TURN IN.
explanation.definitionFit: An investment that brings in a profit is yielding or returning money.

clue.text: There's soupy stuff in this river out of industrial town

indicators.note: out of means the river letter is removed from the town

parts.note: Stockport is an industrial town near Manchester

explanation.surface: A river near a factory town is full of murky gunk.
explanation.walkthrough: STOCKPORT is a former mill town in Greater Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: A large pot in which bones and vegetables simmer to make stock holds soupy liquid.

clue.text: Drill that may help one trying to get gold

definitions.text: Drill that may help one trying to get gold

parts.words: Drill that may help one trying to get gold
parts.note: the gold is the centre of an archery target, and a drill is a practice session rather than a mining tool

explanation.surface: A prospector's drill might help in the search for gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drill' and 'gold' suggest mining, but in archery the inner gold ring is the bullseye.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeated shooting at a target is the drill an archer uses to learn to hit the central gold.

clue.text: Final farewell to sailor meets with the heartless reply

parts.note: RIP (rest in peace) is the final farewell on a gravestone
OS is an ordinary seaman

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word is removed

explanation.surface: A sailor's last goodbye is answered with a cold retort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the middle H out of THE to give TE; 'meets with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick, sharp return in words, a retort or reply.

clue.text: Close agreement, in woman's case

definitions.meaning: packed close, dense; also a pact or agreement
a small case holding face powder and a mirror

explanation.definitionFit: The word means dense, a formal pact, and a woman's powder case with a mirror.

clue.text: Surrounded by noise, individual becomes exhausted

indicators.note: surrounded by means the individual sits inside the noise

parts.note: a din is a loud noise
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: A person amid all the racket ends up worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Being worn out, tired to the point of collapse, is idiomatically being exhausted.

clue.text: Islands could see rebel seizing power at any time

indicators.note: seizing means one piece grabs and holds another inside it

parts.note: Jack Cade led a rebellion in Kent in 1450
P is the abbreviation for power in physics
ever means at any time

explanation.surface: A group of islands might witness a rebel taking control whenever he likes.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Cade led the Kentish revolt of 1450 against Henry VI.
explanation.definitionFit: This Atlantic nation off West Africa is an archipelago, a chain of islands.

clue.text: Lover generally goes over the edge here

indicators.note: goes over means the answer runs across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: A lover usually tips over the brink at this point.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles 'Lover' and 'generally'.
explanation.definitionFit: The verge is the edge or brink of something, as of a road.

clue.text: See love offered by suitor

parts.note: the Holy See, the Pope's seat, is in Rome
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A suitor's love is on show.
explanation.walkthrough: A See is a bishop's seat; the Holy See is Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's young lover gave his name to any ardent wooer or suitor.

clue.text: Bill has no time for a pseud

indicators.note: has no means a piece is dropped from the word before it

parts.note: a bill is a poster stuck on a wall

explanation.surface: Bill can't be bothered with pretentious people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name; it is a printed notice.
explanation.definitionFit: A pseud is a pretentious person putting on airs, someone who strikes attitudes for effect.

clue.text: Base subject will be given this for sentence

definitions.meaning: to ... an argument on something is to base it on that

definitions.text: subject will be given this for sentence
definitions.meaning: in grammar a sentence is a subject plus the part saying something about it

explanation.surface: A lowly prisoner will receive this as punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base subject' and 'sentence' paint a criminal in the dock; the grammar sense is the real one.
explanation.definitionFit: To predicate means to found or base, and the grammatical term is the part of a sentence beyond its subject.

clue.text: Office workers step on stage

explanation.definitionFit: Personal assistants are office workers, and in ballet a single step is called by the French word.

clue.text: The ones here to meet American hero

parts.note: these means the ones here

explanation.surface: The people present are to be introduced to an American champion.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek hero who slew the Minotaur is a legendary champion.

clue.text: One of Saturn's satellites said to contract

indicators.note: said asks for a word that sounds like the satellite's name

parts.note: Titan is Saturn's largest moon

explanation.surface: A moon of Saturn is reportedly shrinking.
explanation.definitionFit: To contract a muscle or grip is to draw it tighter.
